episode_title: MarTech Consulting: Scope Creep, Pricing & Project Management with Kelly Jo Horton
question: How should MarTech consultants handle scope creep when charging by project rather than hourly rates?
transcript_excerpt: Kelly Jo Horton recommends getting ahead of scope creep as best as possible, especially within the first 10 days of a business relationship. When clients request work outside the original scope of work, she creates addendums to SOWs for tasks that will take significant additional time. She also emphasizes the importance of discovery calls before accepting an SOW to identify all work needed upfront, though she notes this often adds items to the initial scope. Being transparent about additional work tasks and offering clients choices—whether to proceed with expanded scope, adjust timeline, or have someone else handle it—is key to managing scope creep.

episode_title: MarTech Consulting: Scope Creep, Pricing & Project Management with Kelly Jo Horton
question: What is the best organizational structure for marketing operations professionals—reporting to systems or marketing leadership?
transcript_excerpt: Kelly Jo prefers sitting in a systems or IT team because it provides technical peers to bounce ideas off and check work, and creates better understanding for implementing governance, process, and accountability. When positioned as a technical resource in a marketing team, she feels like a fish out of water because marketing staff don't understand technical language and generally don't work in agile sprint environments the way engineering teams do. Systems organizations show more appreciation for successful integrations and clean data, whereas marketing teams struggle to understand why technical work takes time and often don't plan for scalability.

episode_title: MarTech Consulting: Scope Creep, Pricing & Project Management with Kelly Jo Horton
question: How do consultants use sprint-based project management to handle competing client requests and prevent overcommitment?
transcript_excerpt: Kelly Jo assigns sprint points to projects and calculates how many points she can complete per week based on meeting time and time needed for reactive emergencies. She builds two-week sprints with prioritized projects, and when new requests come in that bump existing work, those projects move to the next sprint. This approach helps her manage capacity and prevents overcommitment because she knows exactly how many points she can deliver based on her availability.

episode_title: MarTech Consulting: Scope Creep, Pricing & Project Management with Kelly Jo Horton
question: Why do time tracking and invoicing represent the biggest challenges for independent MarTech consultants?
transcript_excerpt: Kelly Jo describes having a visceral emotional reaction to logging time, finding it frustrating to track every minute of every day as an independent consultant. She notes this is particularly difficult because she works in fragmented time blocks, jumping between different clients throughout the day rather than dedicating long focused periods to one client. While FreshBooks offers a built-in timer tool, it only works for dedicated chunks of time for one client at a time, which doesn't match her working style.

episode_title: MarTech Consulting: Scope Creep, Pricing & Project Management with Kelly Jo Horton
question: What is the key difference in influence and decision-making authority between consulting roles and in-house positions?
transcript_excerpt: As a consultant, Kelly Jo acts as an influencer rather than a decision-maker, making recommendations that clients can reject even though they hired her for expertise. Companies ultimately make final decisions and she must implement their preferred approach even if she believes it's not the best way. In contrast, when sitting outside the company as a consultant, her different opinions are sometimes more respected and she finds it easier to speak up and be opinionated, whereas as an employee she would often quiet her opinions knowing conflicting business initiatives and directions.
